help: The functions that sort, format and split text by the rules of a language and region. The other classes in `Novis\Intl` call them for you, so most programs use those classes instead.

methods.name: collateOrder

params.name: options
params.type: { strength?: Strength, caseFirst?: CaseFirst, numeric?: bool, ignorePunctuation?: bool }

methods.help: Sorts strings by the rules of a locale. Returns the indexes of the strings in sorted order. Equal strings keep their order.

methods.name: sortKeys

params.name: options
params.type: { strength?: Strength, caseFirst?: CaseFirst, numeric?: bool, ignorePunctuation?: bool }

methods.help: Returns one sort key for each string. Two keys compare byte by byte in the same order as their strings sort in the locale.

methods.name: formatNumbers

params.name: options
params.type: { style: Style, minFractionDigits: ?uint, maxFractionDigits: ?uint, grouping: ?bool, currency: ?string, currencyDisplay: ?CurrencyDisplay, compactDisplay: ?CompactDisplay }

methods.help: Formats numbers, each given as its decimal text, in the style and locale you give.

methods.name: pluralCategories
methods.help: Returns the plural category of each number, each given as its decimal text, in the locale.

methods.name: formatDateTimes

params.name: values
params.type: array<{ year: int, month: int, day: int, hour: int, minute: int, second: int, nanos: int, offsetSeconds: int, zone: string }>

params.name: options
params.type: { length?: Length, fields?: Fields, seconds?: bool, zone?: ZoneStyle }

methods.help: Formats dates with times of day, each given as its local fields, its UTC offset and its time zone, in the locale.

methods.name: formatDates
methods.help: Formats calendar dates in the locale, with the parts of each date that `fields` names.

methods.name: formatTimes
methods.help: Formats times of day in the locale.

methods.name: formatRelative
methods.help: Formats amounts of time before or after now, such as "in 3 days". A negative count is in the past.

methods.name: formatLists
methods.help: Joins the items of each list with the words of the locale, such as "a, b and c".

methods.name: wordSegments
methods.help: Splits each string into words, spaces and punctuation. Joined again, the parts of a string are the string.

methods.name: sentenceSegments
methods.help: Splits each string into sentences. Joined again, the sentences of a string are the string.

methods.name: resolveLocales
methods.help: Returns, for each locale tag, the locale whose data is used for the service. `und` means only the general rules are used.

methods.name: negotiate
methods.help: Returns the best of the offered locales for an `Accept-Language` header value. If no offered locale matches, it returns the default.

enums.name: Strength
enums.help: Which differences between two strings count when `Collator` sorts them. `Collator` sorts strings by the rules of a language. `Primary` compares the letters only, so "resume" and "Résumé" are equal. `Secondary` also compares accents. `Tertiary` also compares upper and lower case. This is the default. `ignorePunctuation` is another option of `Collator`. When it is `true`, `Primary`, `Secondary` and `Tertiary` do not compare punctuation. `Quaternary` also compares that punctuation. `Identical` also compares the characters themselves when everything else is equal.

enums.name: CaseFirst
enums.help: Whether uppercase or lowercase letters come first when `Collator` sorts words that differ only in case. `Collator` sorts strings by the rules of a language. `Off` is the default. It follows the rules of the language. In English, it puts "apple" before "Apple". `Upper` puts "Apple" first. `Lower` puts "apple" first.

enums.name: Style
enums.help: How `Icu::formatNumbers` writes a number. Each `NumberFormat` method uses one style. `Decimal` writes a plain number, such as "1,234.5" in English. `Percent` multiplies the number by 100 and writes a percentage, so 0.25 is "25%". `Currency` writes an amount of money, such as "$19.90". `Compact` writes a large number in a short form, such as "1.2K" for 1,200.

enums.name: CurrencyDisplay
enums.help: How `NumberFormat::currency` writes the currency of an amount. `Symbol` writes the usual symbol of the language and region. This is the default. In Canada, "$" means Canadian dollars. So in English for Canada, 19.90 US dollars are written "US$19.90". `Narrow` writes the shortest symbol, such as "$19.90". A reader may not know which dollar it is. `Name` writes the name of the currency, such as "19.90 US dollars".

enums.name: CompactDisplay
enums.help: How a compact number is written. A compact number is a large number written short, such as "1.2K" for 1,200. `Short` writes "1.2K" and is the default. `Long` writes "1.2 thousand".

enums.name: Kind
enums.help: Which plural rules `Icu::pluralCategories` uses. `Cardinal` uses the rules for counting, such as "3 items". `Ordinal` uses the rules for places, such as "3rd".

enums.name: Category
enums.help: A plural category of the locale: `Zero`, `One`, `Two`, `Few`, `Many` or `Other`. Each language uses some of them. English counting uses `One` for 1 and `Other` for every other number. `PluralRules` returns these as `Core\Cldr::PluralCategory`.

enums.name: Length
enums.help: How long a formatted date is. For March 1, 2026 in English for the United States, `Short` writes "3/1/26". `Medium` writes "Mar 1, 2026". This is the default. `Long` writes "March 1, 2026". `Long` is the longest length. To also show the day of the week, set `fields` to `Fields::YearMonthDayWeekday`.

enums.name: Fields
enums.help: Which parts of a date `DateFormat::dates` and `DateFormat::dateTimes` show. Each case is named after the parts it shows. The locale decides the order of the parts. A locale is a language and region, such as `en-US` or `de` for German. These examples use `Length::Long` and `en-US`. `Day` shows the day of the month, such as "5". `MonthDay` shows the month and the day, such as "January 5". `YearMonthDay` shows the year, the month and the day, such as "January 5, 2026". This is the default. `Weekday` shows the day of the week, such as "Monday". `DayWeekday` shows the day of the month and the day of the week, such as "5 Monday". `MonthDayWeekday` shows the month, the day and the day of the week, such as "Monday, January 5". `YearMonthDayWeekday` shows all four parts, such as "Monday, January 5, 2026". `Month` shows the month, such as "January". `YearMonth` shows the month and the year, such as "January 2026". In `de`, this is "Januar 2026". `Year` shows the year, such as "2026". `Month`, `YearMonth` and `Year` have no day. A time of day needs a day, so `DateFormat::dateTimes` throws a `LogicError` for these three cases.

enums.name: ZoneStyle
enums.help: How `DateFormat::dateTimes` shows the time zone of a date and time. `None` shows no time zone. This is the default. `Offset` shows the difference from UTC, such as "GMT+2". `Location` shows the country or city of the zone. For the zone `Europe/Vienna`, this is "Austria Time". `Generic` shows the general name of the zone, such as "Central European Time". It does not say whether it is summer time, so the name is the same in summer and in winter.

enums.name: Unit
enums.help: The unit of time that `RelativeTime::format` writes. `RelativeTime::format` writes a count of a unit as a time before or after now. A count of -2 with `Week` gives "2 weeks ago". A positive count is in the future. `Quarter` is three months.

enums.name: Width
enums.help: How short `RelativeTime::format` and `ListFormat::join` make their text. `Wide` writes every word in full: "3 months ago" and "Shop, Blog, and Wiki". This is the default. `Short` uses short forms: "3 mo. ago" and "Shop, Blog, & Wiki". `Narrow` uses the shortest forms: "3mo ago" and "Shop, Blog, Wiki".

enums.name: Numeric
enums.help: Whether `RelativeTime::format` always writes a number. `RelativeTime::format` writes a time before or after now, such as "in 1 day". `Always` writes the counts -1, 0 and 1 of `Day` as "1 day ago", "in 0 days" and "in 1 day". This is the default. `Auto` writes the same counts as "yesterday", "today" and "tomorrow". Most counts have no word like these, such as the count 5. For such a count, `Auto` also writes the number: "in 5 days".

enums.name: Type
enums.help: The words that `ListFormat::join` uses to join the items of a list. `And` writes "tea, coffee, and water" in English. This is the default. `Or` writes "tea, coffee, or water". `Unit` joins the parts of one amount, such as "5 feet, 11 inches".

enums.name: Service
enums.help: The kind of data that `Locale::resolve` checks. For each locale tag, such as `de-AT` for German in Austria, it returns the locale whose data is used. `Collation` is the data for sorting text. `Numbers` is the data for writing numbers. `Plurals` is the data for plural forms. `Dates` is the data for writing dates. `RelativeTime` is the data for times such as "in 3 days". `Lists` is the data for joining lists. `Segmentation` is the data for splitting text into words.
